notes: κατ' ἰδίαν kept as one noncompositional unit on 'apart', headed on ἰδίαν per rule 45's governed-word head; this matches the identical phrase at MAT.17.19, so the chapter writes one analysis and not two (rule 24).
'taketh with him' kept whole on παραλαμβάνει: no Greek preposition is expressed, so rule 36 gives 'with' nowhere else to go, and 'him' is the ordinary rule 7 helper the English idiom requires.
Both articles before names left unrepresented (rule 23); the article before ἀδελφόν is emptied by the possessive that belongs to αὐτοῦ (rule 20), not by rule 23.
ὄρος takes the discontinuous 'a … mountain' with ὑψηλόν bare, per rule 58's anarthrous adjective-plus-noun clause.
